title: In-App Update Runtime Truth, Durable Admission, Helper Migration and Permission Safety Closeout
summary: Completes the accepted Stage 6.6.0 and cumulative Stage 6.6.0.1.2 dofix line with restart-tolerant operator truth, durable exactly-once update admission, strict authority parsing and an automatic legacy helper migration bridge. Update apply now preserves submission replay, audit and terminal evidence across concurrency, crashes and restarts; public API and UI surfaces remain bounded and sanitized; legacy helpers gain ACL-capable handoff without replacing the active owner; and the product tree is fail-closed against unsafe modes, ACLs, symlinks or incomplete permission inspection on GNU, BusyBox and the working NAS.
changelog: Composes update-check truth and active execution truth without false failure during bounded API restarts.
Replaces native confirmation with a localized product modal and keeps reconnect polling free of raw proxy responses.
Adds server-issued submission proofs and a durable bounded admission ledger with exactly-once request and audit identity.
Serializes concurrent apply, cancel and helper claims while preserving deterministic replay through crash boundaries.
Rejects duplicate keys, non-finite JSON, excessive nesting, coerced scalars and contradictory terminal authority.
Sanitizes validation errors and update status so raw values, internal paths, HTML and sensitive fields do not reach users.
Keeps strict API/helper parity for current and legacy read-only evidence without letting legacy shapes authorize new work.
Adds automatic legacy update-helper bootstrap and post-terminal image handoff without replacing the active request owner.
Verifies exact helper image identity, terminal commit evidence, top-level authority and lease release before activation.
Adds complete pre-mutation owner, symlink, mode and ACL inventory for privileged product source paths.
Normalizes only product source to explicit 0755/0644 modes while preserving data, environment and service artifacts.
Fails closed on incomplete find, stat or getfacl inspection and rejects writable named or default ACLs before mutation.
Clears special mode bits across GNU and BusyBox and parses ACL authority only from validated permission fields.
Integrates permission checks into install, update, release preparation, helper images and API bootstrap dependencies.
